paper_title: The Grenoble Axion Haloscope platform (GrAHal): development plan and first results
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on y-axis
notes: First results from the Grenoble Axion Haloscope (GrAHal) pathfinding run at liquid He temperature. The exclusion limit g_agamma ≤ 2.2 × 10^-13 GeV^-1 is set at 6.375 GHz, corresponding to an axion mass of 26.37 μeV (2.637 × 10^-5 eV). The paper explicitly states this is a new exclusion limit with 95% confidence, assuming axions constitute all of the local dark matter density (standard assumption ρ_a = 0.3 GeV/cm^3 for galactic halo). The limit is also expressed relative to the KSVZ benchmark as g_agamma ≤ 22 × g_KSVZ. The cavity parameters: Q0 = 37000, β = 1.2, C = 0.69 for TM010 mode; 14 Tesla magnet; copper cavity (36 mm inner diameter, 150 mm length). This is a haloscope experiment searching for axion dark matter via resonant conversion to photons in an RF cavity. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.75, 32)) | Vision: FIG. 2 shows exclusion limits for axion-photon coupling vs axion mass. The plot displays the cyan band bounded by KSVZ (upper) and DFSZ (lower) theoretical models. The GrAHal first result (vertical purple dashed line at 6.375 GHz, corresponding to 26.37 μeV axion mass) is shown. The lower boundary of the exclusion region (where GrAHal and other experiments set limits) traces a shallow minimum around 3-5 × 10^-5 eV, with coupling values near 8.9-9.0 × 10^-16 GeV^-1. The boundary rises steeply at lower masses (below 1 μeV) and more gradually at higher masses. Sampling density increased near the minimum (around 3-5 × 10^-5 eV) where the slope changes. The GrAHal pathfinding run achieved g_agamma ≤ 22 × 10^-15 GeV^-1 (2.2 × 10^-14 GeV^-1) at 26.37 μeV, which is above the theoretical models shown but represents early prototype performance. | Calibration: No calibration needed
